title: Multi-order Differential Neural Network for TCAD Simulation of the Semiconductor Devices
problem: TCAD requires solving coupled Poisson and drift-diffusion equations to simulate semiconductor device behavior. Traditional discretization methods (finite volume and finite element) are computationally expensive and burden computing resources.
motivation: TCAD is crucial for semiconductor device design and manufacturing; reducing computational burden while maintaining accuracy is essential for efficient device optimization.
method: Proposes a Physics-Informed Neural Network (PINN) approach using a multi-order differential neural network (MDNN), an improved Radial Basis Function Neural Network (RBFNN). The method trains to achieve coupled solutions of Poisson and drift-diffusion equations under steady-state conditions without requiring pre-existing training datasets by directly incorporating physical constraints into the network.
key_novelty: First TCAD simulation method using PINNs that requires no pre-existing training data, achieving self-consistent solutions of coupled physical equations.
contributions: Novel multi-order differential neural network (MDNN) architecture based on improved RBFNN for physics-informed simulation
First PINN-based TCAD simulation eliminating the need for pre-existing datasets
Self-consistent solution of coupled Poisson and drift-diffusion equations under steady-state conditions
Demonstration on PN junction diode achieving sub-10^-5 solution error
limitations: Not discussed; scalability to complex 3D device geometries and detailed computational efficiency comparison with traditional TCAD methods not provided.
primary_theme: Physics-informed neural networks for TCAD simulation
